title: オーディオAIにおけるアーキテクチャの分断：マルチステージ・リファインメント対エンドツーエンドの融合
titleEn: The Architectural Divide in Audio AI: Multi-Stage Refinement versus End-to-End Fusion
dek: 音声分離およびオーディオ生成の領域における、モジュール式カスケードパイプラインと、統合・内部融合されたニューラルネットワークの批判的評価。
dekEn: A critical evaluation of modular cascading pipelines versus unified, internally fused neural networks in the landscape of speech separation and audio generation.
summaryEn: This research feature explores the fundamental architectural divide in modern speech and audio processing: the debate between multi-stage cascading pipelines and unified end-to-end deep learning models. By examining empirical evidence from recent DCASE challenges, generative flow-matching methods, and adaptive feature-gating techniques, we outline the trade-offs of each approach. While multi-stage pipelines offer modular auditability and step-by-step refinement, they face high computational overhead and latency during inference. Conversely, unified networks with adaptive feature-level fusion reduce error propagation and latency but present training complexities. Ultimately, this feature provides practitioners with key guidelines to navigate these paradigms under real-world computational constraints.
keyPointsEn: Multi-stage refinement relies on sequential task execution to isolate components, allowing targeted semantic and acoustic adjustments.
End-to-end fusion minimizes error propagation and information loss by utilizing internal gating mechanisms to merge semantic and spatial features.
Real-world deployment constraints force a critical trade-off between the modular auditability of pipelines and the low-latency efficiency of unified networks.

perspectives.label: マルチステージ・リファインメントとポストプロセッシング
perspectives.description: 個々のコンポーネントの監査可能性とパフォーマンスを最大化するために、カスケードされたモジュール操作、シーケンシャルなリファインメント、および個別のポストプロセッシング層に焦点を当てる。
perspectives.descriptionEn: Focuses on cascading modular operations, sequential refinement, and discrete post-processing layers to maximize the auditability and performance of individual components.

perspectives.label: エンドツーエンドのアーキテクチャ融合
perspectives.description: 統合されたアーキテクチャ内での直接的な最適化を提唱し、高度な内部ゲーティングを活用してセマンティックな詳細と空間的な詳細を融合させ、カスケードエラーを最小限に抑える。
perspectives.descriptionEn: Advocates for direct optimization within unified architectures, leveraging advanced internal gating to fuse semantic and spatial details while minimizing cascade errors.

perspectives.label: 実用的なデプロイメントと効率性の制約
perspectives.description: ターゲットハードウェアプラットフォームにおける、モデルの複雑さ、推論レイテンシ、および計算フットプリントの間の実用的な妥協点を分析する。
perspectives.descriptionEn: Analyzes the practical compromises between model complexity, inference latency, and computational footprint on target hardware platforms.

sections.heading: 現代のオーディオAIの展望
sections.headingEn: The Landscape of Modern Audio AI

blocks.text: 現代の音声・音響人工知能の状況は、根本的なアーキテクチャの緊張によって特徴付けられています。すなわち、複雑なタスクを逐次的な多段階パイプラインで解決するか、統一されたエンドツーエンドのディープラーニングモデルに依存するかという点です。空間的な音源分離や音楽生成、多チャンネル音響シーンのセグメンテーションなどのタスクにおいて、研究者は処理チェーンの構造を選択しなければなりません [S1, S3]。一方では、現代のフレームワークは分離モデルと分類モデルを連続する段階で組み合わせ、低レベルの音響的・意味的クラスの手がかりを用いて推定出力を段階的に精緻化することが多いです [S3]。他方、条件付きフローマッチングによる音声分離 [S4] や、Ambisonicsベースの空間認識型エンドツーエンドモデル [S6] など、高度な生成的フレームワークの登場によって、統一ネットワークの限界が押し広げられています。同様に、合唱アンサンブル分離のような専門領域では、スペクトル成分の重複が課題となり、特定の基本周波数輪郭を組み込んだエンドツーエンドアーキテクチャへの移行が歴史的に促されてきました [S7]。この技術的な分岐は、現代の音響アーキテクチャにおける最適なモジュール化レベルについての未解決の議論を浮き彫りにしています。
blocks.textEn: The landscape of contemporary speech and audio artificial intelligence is defined by a fundamental architectural tension: whether to resolve complex tasks using sequential, multi-stage pipelines or to rely on unified, end-to-end deep learning models. In tasks ranging from spatial source separation and music generation to multi-channel sound scene segmentation, researchers must choose how to structure their processing chains [S1, S3]. On one hand, modern frameworks often couple separate separation and classification models across successive stages, using low-level acoustic and semantic class clues to progressively refine estimated outputs [S3]. On the other hand, the advent of sophisticated generative frameworks, such as conditional flow matching for speech separation [S4], along with spatial-aware end-to-end models like Ambisonics-based architectures [S6], has pushed the boundaries of unified networks. Similarly, specialized domains like choral ensemble separation struggle with overlapping spectral components, historically prompting a move towards end-to-end architectures tailored with specific fundamental frequency contours [S7]. This technological divergence highlights the unresolved debate regarding the optimal level of modularity in modern audio architectures.

sections.heading: 分断されたパラダイム：モジュール式リファインメント対統合された集約
sections.headingEn: Divided Paradigms: Modular Refinement vs. Unified Integration

blocks.text: 多段階精緻化の支持者は、音声信号の分離、クラス依存の後処理パラメータの適用、人間の好み指標による精緻化など、明確なサブタスクを分離することで、各コンポーネントの監査性と性能を最大化できると主張しています [S1, S3, S8]。このパラダイムでは、クラスの手がかりや特殊なフィルターを用いて、離散的な境界でエラーを緩和することが可能です [S3, S8]。一方、エンドツーエンドのアーキテクチャ統合の支持者は、独立したモデルを連鎖させると、壊滅的なエラー伝播が生じると主張します。彼らは、手作業で設計されたスペクトログラム表現に頼るのではなく、生の波形領域で直接動作する単一ネットワーク内で直接最適化することで、重要な位相情報を保持し、情報損失を防げると論じています [S5]。外部のヒューリスティックな後処理を用いるのではなく、エンドツーエンド支持者は内部の特徴レベルでの融合に注力します [S2]。新しいゲーティングパラダイムを用いて、デコーダ構造内で差分ベースのアテンションを直接計算することで、統一ネットワークは表現の不一致を内部で解決し、離散的な外部精緻化段階を完全に不要にすることができます [S2]。
blocks.textEn: Proponents of multi-stage refinement argue that isolating distinct sub-tasks—such as separating audio signals, applying class-dependent post-processing parameters, and refining with human preference metrics—maximizes the auditability and performance of each individual component [S1, S3, S8]. Under this paradigm, errors can be mitigated at discrete boundaries using class clues or specialized filters [S3, S8]. Conversely, advocates for end-to-end architectural fusion assert that cascading independent models causes catastrophic error propagation. They argue that direct optimization within a single network, operating directly in the raw waveform domain rather than relying on hand-crafted spectrogram representations, preserves critical phase information and prevents information loss [S5]. Rather than employing external heuristic post-processing, end-to-end advocates focus on internal feature-level fusion [S2]. By employing novel gating paradigms that calculate difference-based attention directly within decoder structures, unified networks can resolve representational discrepancies internally, avoiding the need for discrete external refinement stages entirely [S2].

sections.heading: ベンチマークから得られた実証的証拠

blocks.text: 最近の競争的ベンチマークから得られる実証的証拠は、両方のパラダイムを支持しています。多段階システムでは、音源分離と意味分類モデルの段階的な結合によって、著しい性能向上が達成されています。例えば、DCASE 2026空間音響シーンセグメンテーションタスクで評価された三段階の自己誘導型精緻化フレームワークは、分離された波形を低レベル音響参照として、クラスラベルを意味的手がかりとして利用し、ベースライン指標を大幅に上回る改善をもたらしました [S3]。同様に、条件付きフローマッチングを用いた生成的音声分離モデルは、凍結された話者エンコーダを用いて置換曖昧性を解決するバイオメトリック選択などの後処理ステップによって恩恵を受けています [S4]。一方、エンドツーエンドアーキテクチャは強力な内部最適化能力を示しています。差分駆動型ゲーティング機構、具体的にはFeature-Difference GatingやEntropy-Difference Gatingは、音声分離タスクにおいて従来のアテンション融合技術よりも優れた性能を示し、逐次的な外部段階を必要としませんでした [S2]。さらに、Wave-U-Netのような初期の波形ベースのエンドツーエンドモデルは、生音声の直接処理によって、従来のスペクトログラムベースのディープラーニングパイプラインと同等かそれ以上の性能を達成できることを示しました [S5]。内部融合が合唱アンサンブルの基本周波数輪郭など領域特有の条件付けと組み合わされると、統一アーキテクチャは顕著な性能上の利点を示します [S7]。
blocks.textEn: Empirical evidence from recent competitive benchmarks supports both paradigms. In multi-stage systems, the progressive coupling of source separation and semantic classification models has achieved substantial performance gains. For example, a three-stage self-guided refinement framework evaluated on the DCASE 2026 spatial sound scene segmentation task utilized separated waveforms as low-level acoustic references and class labels as semantic clues, leading to a dramatic improvement over baseline metrics [S3]. Similarly, generative speech separation models using conditional flow matching benefit from post-processing steps like biometric selection, which utilizes a frozen speaker encoder to resolve permutation ambiguity [S4]. On the other hand, end-to-end architectures demonstrate powerful internal optimization capabilities. Difference-driven gating mechanisms, specifically Feature-Difference Gating and Entropy-Difference Gating, have outperformed conventional attention fusion techniques on speech separation tasks without requiring sequential external stages [S2]. Furthermore, early waveform-based end-to-end models like Wave-U-Net demonstrated that direct processing of raw audio can match or exceed traditional spectrogram-based deep learning pipelines [S5]. When internal fusion is coupled with domain-specific conditioning, such as fundamental frequency contours for choir ensembles, unified architectures show significant performance advantages [S7].

blocks.text: これらのパラダイムを評価する際の未解決の課題は、客観的な分離ベンチマークと主観的な音質や下流での有用性との間に存在するギャップにあります。Scale-Invariant Signal-to-Distortion Ratio（SI-SDR）やPerceptual Evaluation of Speech Quality（PESQ）といった標準的な指標は、正確な数値評価を提供しますが、音声認識や話者認証のような下流アプリケーションでの性能を直接的には捉えていません。これらの下流タスクは、cpWERやEERといった別の指標で評価されます [S4]。テキストから音楽生成の分野では、ラウドネス正規化や音源分離といった多段階の推論後処理が有効ですが、最も品質に寄与しているのは、トップパフォーマンスのサンプルに対する専門家によるイテレーションであり、音声とテキストの整合性を高めるための好み調整パスは、ノイズレベル程度の改善しかもたらさない場合があります [S1]。さらに、音イベント検出の研究では、音声イベントの境界を特定するために用いられる後処理アルゴリズムが極めて重要な影響を持つことが強調されています [S8]。クラス依存のパラメトリック後処理を調整すると、性能指標が大きく変動することがあり、これは時間的なセグメンテーションや境界の定義方法によって実験結果が大きく左右されることを示しています [S8]。このことは、システムの実証的な比較が、テスト時に後処理の変数をどのように分離するかに大きく依存する場合があることを示唆しています。
blocks.textEn: An unresolved challenge in evaluating these paradigms lies in the discrepancy between objective separation benchmarks and subjective audio quality or downstream utility. Standard metrics like Scale-Invariant Signal-to-Distortion Ratio (SI-SDR) and Perceptual Evaluation of Speech Quality (PESQ) offer precise numeric evaluations but do not directly capture performance in downstream applications such as speech recognition and speaker verification, which are instead evaluated via metrics like cpWER and EER [S4]. In text-to-music generation, multi-stage inference post-processing like loudness normalization and source separation helps, but expert iteration on top-performing samples serves as the dominant contributor to quality, whereas the preference-tuning pass for audio-text alignment may only provide noise-level gains [S1]. Furthermore, studies in sound event detection emphasize the crucial impact of the post-processing algorithms used to identify audio event boundaries [S8]. When class-dependent parametric post-processing is adjusted, performance metrics can fluctuate substantially, highlighting how empirical results can be heavily influenced by how temporal segmentation and boundaries are defined [S8]. This indicates that empirical comparisons of systems can sometimes depend heavily on how post-processing variables are isolated during testing.

sections.heading: 実務家への影響とデプロイメントの現実

blocks.text: 実務者やシステムエンジニアにとって、適切なアーキテクチャを選択するには、タスク性能と実際の運用効率との間で慎重なトレードオフが求められます。特に反復的な洗練ループや生成的なベスト・オブ・N候補サンプリングを含む多段階パイプラインは、計算負荷や遅延が大きく、リアルタイムのエッジデバイスでの運用がより困難になります [S1, S4]。一方で、空間選択や適応的な特徴レベルのゲーティングをネットワーク内に直接統合した統一型のエンドツーエンドシステムは、誤差の伝播や処理段階の分離を回避できます [S2, S6]。しかし、こうした統合型ネットワークはブラックボックス的な不透明性を持つため、モジュラー設計と比べて複雑な音響環境で特定の失敗をデバッグするのが難しくなることがあります。絶対的な精度やモジュールごとの監査性が最重要であり、計算遅延が二次的な場合には、意味的・音響的フィードバックループを組み合わせた多段階フレームワークが依然として強力なエンジニアリング選択肢となります [S3]。
blocks.textEn: For practitioners and system engineers, selecting the correct architecture requires a careful trade-off between task performance and real-world deployment efficiency. Multi-stage pipelines, particularly those involving iterative refinement loops or generative best-of-N candidate sampling, impose substantial computational overhead and latency, making them more challenging for real-time edge devices [S1, S4]. In contrast, unified end-to-end systems that integrate spatial selection or adaptive feature-level gating directly within the network avoid cascading error propagation and separate processing stages [S2, S6]. However, these integrated networks can suffer from black-box opacity, making it difficult to debug specific failures in complex acoustic environments compared to modular designs. When absolute precision and modular auditability are paramount, and computational latency is secondary, multi-stage frameworks utilizing joint semantic and acoustic feedback loops remain a powerful engineering choice [S3].

sections.heading: オーディオ処理の未来の展望

blocks.text: 音声処理の未来は、先進的な表現融合とスケーラブルな生成モデルによって推進される、これら二つのパラダイムの収束にあります。注目すべき主な分野としては、複雑なマルチスケール特徴融合を多様なモダリティ間で扱うための差分駆動型ゲーティング機構の応用や、高度に事前学習されたセマンティックエンコーダを下流の分離タスクに直接統合することが挙げられます [S2, S3]。フローマッチングや拡散モデルが成熟を続ける中、生成的サンプリング戦略の計算遅延を削減することが、商用リアルタイム音声システムへの統合に不可欠となるでしょう [S4]。さらに、基盤モデルがより豊かな音響的・意味的表現を提供するようになるにつれ、明示的な多段階パイプラインと暗黙的な特徴融合の境界は曖昧になり、両者の利点を兼ね備えたハイブリッドアーキテクチャが登場すると予想されます。
blocks.textEn: The future of audio processing lies in the convergence of these two paradigms, driven by advanced representational fusion and scalable generative modeling. Key areas to monitor include the application of difference-driven gating mechanisms to handle complex multi-scale feature fusion across diverse modalities and the integration of highly pretrained semantic encoders directly into downstream separation tasks [S2, S3]. As flow matching and diffusion models continue to mature, reducing the computational latency of generative sampling strategies will be essential for their integration into commercial real-time audio systems [S4]. Additionally, as foundational models provide richer acoustic and semantic representations, the boundaries between explicit multi-stage pipelines and implicit feature fusion are expected to blur, giving rise to hybrid architectures that capture the benefits of both worlds.

sources.title: Improving Text-to-Music Generation with Human Preference Rewards
sources.abstract: We describe our entry to the efficiency track of the Academic Text-to-Music (ATTM) Grand Challenge at ICME 2026. Beyond the challenge protocol's FAD-CLAP and CLAP score, we add a learned human-preference reward from TuneJury, a twin pairwise ranker trained over open music-preference datasets. The reward serves both as a training-time conditioning signal and as a sample-selection criterion. The pipeline combines five engineering decisions on a 120M-parameter FluxAudio-S backbone, four at training time and one at inference: (i) training-time reward conditioning that doubles as an inference-time CFG axis, (ii) a sweep over five score-conditioning architectures, where training and inference use different variants, (iii) expert iteration on the top decile, (iv) a short preference-tuning pass (CRPO) for audio-text alignment, and (v) inference post-processing via joint CFG, source separation, and loudness normalization. Per-stage decomposition on 100 Song Describer prompts shows training-time reward conditioning as a functional conditioning axis, expert iteration as the dominant contributor, the preference-tuning pass adding only noise-level gain, and the inference-time score scalar already saturated by the end of the chain.

sources.title: Difference-Driven Gating: Adaptive Feature Fusion for U-Net Decoder
sources.abstract: The U-Net style models have been widely used in many applications. A critical step in these models is to reconstruct the lower-level features using a top-down decoder. This reconstruction requires precise fusion of high-level semantics and low-level details. Existing attention-based fusion methods typically derive attention weights from the top-down decoder features (global) alone or the correlation between the top-down decoder features and the bottom-up encoder features (local), then modulate the encoder features using these weights. In this work, we explore a different paradigm: deriving attention weights from the difference between the two feature streams. To this end, we propose two difference-based gating approaches: Feature-difference gating (FDG), which directly uses the absolute difference between global and local features to generate adaptive gating maps, and Entropy-difference gating (EDG), which measures the representational certainty of each stream via information entropy and uses their signed entropy difference to derive the attention weights. Both methods produce coupled gating maps that simultaneously modulate the global and local features. Experiments on different tasks including medical image segmentation, remote sensing image cloud removal and speech separation showed that both methods outperformed existing attention-based fusion methods, and EDG performed better. The results suggested a new paradigm for multi-scale feature fusion in the U-Net style structures.

sources.title: A Multi-Stage Separation-and-Classification Framework Guided by Complementary Acoustic-to-Semantic Clues
sources.abstract: This report describes the system proposed for the DCASE 2026 Challenge Task 4: Spatial Semantic Segmentation of Sound Scenes (S5). Specifically, we develop a multi-stage framework in which each stage couples a separation model with a classification model. The first stage performs source separation and classification directly on the multi-channel mixture. Its outputs are then propagated to the following stage as two complementary clues that progressively refine each target estimate: (i) an enrollment clue, the separated waveform itself, serving as a low-level acoustic reference; and (ii) a class clue, the predicted label encoded as a one-hot vector. The third stage reuses the second-stage outputs under the same scheme, forming an iterative self-guided refinement process. In addition, we use a fine-grained frame-level audio embedding from an audio encoder pretrained on a large audio corpus as an additional clue to further improve the audio separation performance. On the test set, the proposed system achieves a CAPI-SDRi of 15.51 dB, a mixture accuracy of 71.09\%, and a source accuracy of 78.62\%; with an improvement of 7.02 dB, 10.38\%p and 8.22\%p compared with the challenge baseline, respectively.

sources.title: Flow Matching-Based Speech Source Separation with Best-of-N Biometric Sampling
sources.abstract: Single-channel speech separation remains challenging for real-world deployment due to source permutation ambiguity, sampling variability of generative models, and the difficulty of processing long recordings with chunk-wise inference. We address these issues with a conditional flow-matching-based method that produces an ordered two-source output conditioned on the mixture. A frozen speaker encoder defines the source order during training and is reused at inference for biometric best-of-$N$ candidate selection and chunk-level channel alignment. We evaluate separation quality on Libri2Mix benchmark using SI-SDR, PESQ, and ESTOI, and measure downstream impact using cpWER for automatic speech recognition and EER for speaker verification. The results show that the proposed Transformer U-Net variant is competitive with strong baselines in objective separation metrics and achieves the lowest downstream automatic speech recognition and speaker verification error rates in all evaluated settings.

sources.title: End-to-end music source separation: is it possible in the waveform domain?
sources.abstract: Most of the currently successful source separation techniques use the magnitude spectrogram as input, and are therefore by default omitting part of the signal: the phase. To avoid omitting potentially useful information, we study the viability of using end-to-end models for music source separation --- which take into account all the information available in the raw audio signal, including the phase. Although during the last decades end-to-end music source separation has been considered almost unattainable, our results confirm that waveform-based models can perform similarly (if not better) than a spectrogram-based deep learning model. Namely: a Wavenet-based model we propose and Wave-U-Net can outperform DeepConvSep, a recent spectrogram-based deep learning model.

sources.title: Direction Specific Ambisonics Source Separation with End-To-End Deep Learning
sources.abstract: Ambisonics is a scene-based spatial audio format that has several useful features compared to object-based formats, such as efficient whole scene rotation and versatility. However, it does not provide direct access to the individual source signals, so that these have to be separated from the mixture when required. Typically, this is done with linear spherical harmonics (SH) beamforming. In this paper, we explore deep-learning-based source separation on static Ambisonics mixtures. In contrast to most source separation approaches, which separate a fixed number of sources of specific sound types, we focus on separating arbitrary sound from specific directions. Specifically, we propose three operating modes that combine a source separation neural network with SH beamforming: refinement, implicit, and mixed mode. We show that a neural network can implicitly associate conditioning directions with the spatial information contained in the Ambisonics scene to extract specific sources. We evaluate the performance of the three proposed approaches and compare them to SH beamforming on musical mixtures generated with the musdb18 dataset, as well as with mixtures generated with the FUSS dataset for universal source separation, under both anechoic and room conditions. Results show that the proposed approaches offer improved separation performance and spatial selectivity compared to conventional SH beamforming.

sources.title: Deep Learning Based Source Separation Applied To Choir Ensembles
sources.abstract: Choral singing is a widely practiced form of ensemble singing wherein a group of people sing simultaneously in polyphonic harmony. The most commonly practiced setting for choir ensembles consists of four parts; Soprano, Alto, Tenor and Bass (SATB), each with its own range of fundamental frequencies (F$0$s). The task of source separation for this choral setting entails separating the SATB mixture into the constituent parts. Source separation for musical mixtures is well studied and many deep learning based methodologies have been proposed for the same. However, most of the research has been focused on a typical case which consists in separating vocal, percussion and bass sources from a mixture, each of which has a distinct spectral structure. In contrast, the simultaneous and harmonic nature of ensemble singing leads to high structural similarity and overlap between the spectral components of the sources in a choral mixture, making source separation for choirs a harder task than the typical case. This, along with the lack of an appropriate consolidated dataset has led to a dearth of research in the field so far. In this paper we first assess how well some of the recently developed methodologies for musical source separation perform for the case of SATB choirs. We then propose a novel domain-specific adaptation for conditioning the recently proposed U-Net architecture for musical source separation using the fundamental frequency contour of each of the singing groups and demonstrate that our proposed approach surpasses results from domain-agnostic architectures.

sources.title: Evaluation of post-processing algorithms for polyphonic sound event detection
sources.abstract: Sound event detection (SED) aims at identifying audio events (audio tagging task) in recordings and then locating them temporally (localization task). This last task ends with the segmentation of the frame-level class predictions, that determines the onsets and offsets of the audio events. Yet, this step is often overlooked in scientific publications. In this paper, we focus on the post-processing algorithms used to identify the audio event boundaries. Different post-processing steps are investigated, through smoothing, thresholding, and optimization. In particular, we evaluate different approaches for temporal segmentation, namely statistic-based and parametric methods. Experiments are carried out on the DCASE 2018 challenge task 4 data. We compared post-processing algorithms on the temporal prediction curves of two models: one based on the challenge's baseline and a Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) model. Results show the crucial impact of the post-processing methods on the final detection score. Statistic-based methods yield a 22.9% event-based F-score on the evaluation set with our MIL model. Moreover, the best results were obtained using class-dependent parametric methods with 32.0% F-score.
